subject: Request: staged traffic isolation + automatic rollback as SLA mitigation
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@astrapay.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@astrapay.com
Date: 2027-03-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Spike after model canary — ask to pause staged traffic

Hi Olga,

We started a canary yesterday that routes 10% of our traffic to the new model variant (redwood-model-v2.0-q4). Within a few hours we saw p95 latency jump ~180ms on authenticated checkouts and a small but measurable increase in 500/503 transient errors. Impact is spiky but repeats across regions. Our ops team is concerned this will breach the 99.9% uptime/latency guarantees in our contract if the rollout continues at current velocity.

Can Redwood implement a traffic holdback for our account (reduce canary to 0% until root cause) and enable an automatic fallback rule so traffic is pinned to the previous model when p95 exceeds a threshold? We need this in place before we attempt another staged rollout — otherwise we have to halt deployments entirely which would delay our roadmap.

Attachments: latency_spike_20270328.png (screenshot of metrics), brief logs snippet.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Head of Platform Ops, AstraPay
amit@astrapay.com

From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@astrapay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-28T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike after model canary — ask to pause staged traffic

Amit,

Thanks for the heads up and for the screenshots — that helps a lot. We can support a couple of mitigations quickly:

- Holdback: immediately reduce canary traffic to 0% for AstraPay (we can do a per-account override).
- Auto-fallback: configure a policy that pins all traffic to the last known-good model when p95 latency increases by X ms for Y minutes.
- Pinning: create a temporary model pin (v1.12) scoped to AstraPay until you’re comfortable re-rolling.

I need SRE and product sign-off on the exact thresholds and the rollback window. Rishi — can you confirm the quickest safe path to add a per-tenant override + an automated rollback trigger? Aditya — I’ll need a short note for the account (and potentially a credit) to keep Procurement in the loop.

I’m attaching our rollout_runbook_v2.pdf which outlines the change process and rollback steps.

Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@astrapay.com>
Cc: procurement@astrapay.com
Date: 2027-03-29T09:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike after model canary — ask to pause staged traffic

Thanks Olga and Amit — looping Procurement to align on any commercial remediation.

Amit, we understand the business urgency. If Redwood implements the holdback and automatic fallback tomorrow, we are prepared to offer a time-limited credit proportional to lost SLO hours while the canary is paused (I will propose 30% credit for affected hours as a starting point). If you can confirm the affected window and when you want us to proceed we’ll generate the amendment and the HubSpot deal will be updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/AST-2027-Q1-54.

Olga — once SRE confirms the rollback thresholds I’ll prepare the amendment and DocuSign link.

—Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@astrapay.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T02:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike after model canary — ask to pause staged traffic

Quick technical plan (safe, reversible):

1) Apply per-tenant traffic override: set AstraPay canary traffic to 0% immediately. This is a config change in the routing service (no model reload).
2) Deploy automated fallback rule scoped to AstraPay:
   - Condition: observed p95 latency for checkout route increases > 300ms relative to baseline AND error rate > 0.5% for window T = 3 minutes.
   - Action: switch routing to pinned model redwood-model-v1.12 for 30 minutes, trigger alert, and start automated diagnostics.
   - Safety: require human-confirm to re-enable canary after automated rollback; can only be cleared by SRE + customer ops.
3) Create an isolated canary namespace for AstraPay for future rollouts (routes, KV caches) so we can run A/B without collateral impact.

I opened INFRA-9845 and attached the patch (INFRA-9845-patch.diff) and a short runbook update (rollout_runbook_v2.pdf). We can schedule the holdback at any time; low-traffic window recommended: 2027-04-06 03:00-04:00 UTC.

Notes: this approach avoids global model pinning and limits blast radius to AstraPay. Auto-fallback is implemented in the routing layer and has been used in two other customers' incidents last year.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

From: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@astrapay.com>, procurement@astrapay.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:42:00Z
Subject: Final: holdback + auto-rollback plan and commercial amendment

Amit — confirming next steps and our decision:

- Action: Redwood will apply a per-tenant holdback for AstraPay at 2027-04-06 03:00 UTC (reduce canary to 0%).
- Auto-rollback policy: enable the p95 > 300ms & error-rate > 0.5% for 3-minute window rule. On trigger we will pin traffic to redwood-model-v1.12 for 30 minutes and notify both teams.
- Isolation: create a dedicated canary namespace for future staged rollouts.
- Commercial: we are proposing a 30% credit for affected SLO hours during the holdback window. A DocuSign amendment is ready: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/amendment-AST-54.

Please reply with a single-line approval ("Approve: implement holdback and amendment") so we can execute the changes and send the DocuSign.
